settlement_source: Official final result per governing league, then ESPN/others in hierarchical order. Kalshi series sources: NCAA (ncaa.com), ESPN. Terms https://assets.kalshi.com/contract_terms/FOOTBALLGAMEWIN.pdf.
settlement_variable: Team X strictly outscores opponent in full regulation incl. all overtime in the specified college football game; first official final result reported (corrections accepted only before Contract Expiration if clearly erroneous).
timezone: Eastern Time (ET) for time periods; API close_time UTC authoritative. Expiration time per terms 10:00 AM ET.
tie_handling: If tied with no Tie strike listed YES and NO each pay $0.50; if Tie strike listed it resolves YES and team strikes NO. (College OT rarely ends tied.)
rounding: n/a (strictly greater score); ties paid per tie clause
trading_close_vs_settlement: API close_time is set days after scheduled game start (sample: game Oct 28 -> close Oct 30 23:00Z), but the contract expires earlier once a winner is reported (Rule 7.2); trading is live in-play. Settlement timer 90s. Last Trading Time = Expiration time.
early_close_or_void_clauses: Postponed but starts within 48 h of original start: stays open, resolves on result. Not started within 48 h / cancelled: last fair price (Exchange sole discretion). Suspended/abandoned before 55 min of play and not resuming within 48 h: last fair price; after 55 min or league declares game final: settle on state at that point. Forfeit before kickoff: last fair price; after kickoff: per official result. Venue change within 48 h same home/away OK; reversed home/away: last fair price. Disqualification/vacated pre-game: last fair price; post-start: NO for DQ'd team. Market Outcome Review at sole discretion (Rule 7.1). can_close_early=1.
title_vs_rules_divergences: Title 'X wins' omits the 48-h postponement/fair-price clause and the 55-minute suspension rule
Fair-price resolution is discretionary, not a $0/$1 payout
Opponent forfeit before kickoff does NOT pay YES

public_feeds_for_settlement_variable.name: ESPN scoreboard / game pages (unofficial JSON endpoints)
public_feeds_for_settlement_variable.latency: approx seconds to tens of seconds (not measured)

toxicity_flags: Outcome revealed in-play while trading stays open: decided/late-game states observable by faster feeds (feed-latency adverse selection)
Web scoreboard latency vs broadcast/stadium creates informed flow
Fair-price (last price) resolution on postponement/cancellation/suspension at Exchange sole discretion
Suspension rule keyed to 55 minutes of play: clock basis ambiguous
Insider prohibitions (players, coaches, staff, owners) imply known information-asymmetry risk
Market Outcome Review (Rule 7.1) at sole discretion; close_time days after game despite early expiration
notes: Read Kalshi series/markets and FOOTBALLGAMEWIN.pdf (middle via cached file). Did not fetch ncaa.com/ESPN pages; latency figures are estimates. 472 open markets; ~$870k 24h volume.
